title: Comparatives 10: Mixed Review (all forms together)
description: The finisher for the track. Every comparative and superlative form meets in one place: the regular -ее, the irregular -е, the чем and bare-genitive 'than', the compound более / менее, and the superlative самый. You spot which form is at work and pick the right one. No new grammar.
descriptionRussian: Итоговый урок трека. Здесь встречаются все формы сравнительной и превосходной степени: регулярное -ее, неправильное -е, «чем» и беспредложный родительный, составное «более / менее» и превосходная степень «самый». Нужно узнать форму и выбрать правильную. Нового материала нет.
intro: Two systems, and the choice between them is mostly about position. A one-word comparative never changes and cannot precede a noun. A two-word one always agrees and can go anywhere. Everything here is one of those two, plus the small closed lists of irregulars that refuse to be either.
rules: Synthetic comparatives are one word and never change form: the regular -ее (новее, интереснее) and the irregular -е with a changed consonant (лучше, дороже, выше).
Say 'than' two ways: чем + the plain subject form (старше, чем брат) or the bare genitive (старше брата). Add the gap with на + a number, a multiplier with в + раз / раза.
The compound более / менее + an agreeing adjective is the only comparative that can sit before a noun: более интересная книга. Менее means 'less'.

The superlative самый + adjective agrees with the noun (самый красивый дом). The formal наиболее / наименее and the literary -ейший / -айший mean the same but are recognise-only at this level. Never stack two markers (не более новее, не самый интереснейший).
examples: Этот дом новее, чем тот. (This house is newer than that one.) Regular synthetic -ее; чем + plain subject form.
Кофе дороже чая. (Coffee is more expensive than tea.) Irregular synthetic дороже; bare-genitive 'than'.
Антон на два года старше брата. (Anton is two years older than his brother.) Irregular старше; на + number gap; bare genitive.
Это более интересная книга. (This is a more interesting book.) Compound более + agreeing adjective before the noun.
Это самый красивый дом в городе. (This is the most beautiful house in the city.) Superlative самый + agreeing adjective.
Наиболее важная задача — закончить проект. (The most important task is to finish the project.) Formal наиболее: recognise its meaning, no need to produce it.

tables.title: The five forms in one place

rows.label: 'Than'
cells: чем + subject form OR bare genitive

patternRecognition.question: Which form is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Новее is the regular synthetic comparative of новый: stem нов- + -ее. One word, invariable, sitting after the subject. The чем + plain subject form (чем тот) marks 'than'.

patternRecognition.question: Which form is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Дороже is the irregular synthetic comparative of дорогой: the stem-final г changes to ж and the suffix is the short -е. The bare genitive чая ('than tea') marks the comparison. The regular -ее would give the non-word дорогее.

patternRecognition.sentence: Это более интересная книга, чем та.
patternRecognition.question: Which form is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Более интересная is the compound comparative: более + the agreeing adjective интересная (feminine, to match книга). It sits before the noun, which the invariable synthetic интереснее cannot do. The word более is the giveaway.

patternRecognition.question: Which form is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Самая старшая is the everyday superlative: самый + an agreeing adjective, both feminine to match Маша. The word самый marks the superlative. Старшая alone would be a plain adjective, and старше would be the comparative; with самый the meaning is 'the oldest of all'.

patternRecognition.question: Which form is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Наиболее is the formal 'most': it builds a superlative, the same meaning as самый важная задача, just in a bookish register. You only need to recognise it. It is invariable, so важная (not наиболее) carries the agreement. It is not a comparative: наиболее means 'the most', not 'more'.

patternRecognition.question: Which form is operating here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Интереснее is the regular synthetic comparative of интересный: stem интересн- + -ее, one word, invariable, in the predicative slot. The чем + plain subject form follows.

items.promptEnglish: This house is newer than that one.
items.hint: Predicative slot, regular synthetic comparative of новый.
items.explanation: Новее is the regular synthetic comparative of новый: stem нов- + -ее, invariable. Never stack two markers (более новее is wrong).

items.promptEnglish: This book is more interesting than the film.
items.hint: Predicative slot, the regular -ее form of интересный.
items.explanation: Интереснее is the regular synthetic comparative of интересный (stem + -ее), invariable, in the predicative slot. Более интереснее is a double comparative, always wrong.

items.promptEnglish: Coffee is more expensive than tea.
items.hint: Irregular synthetic comparative of дорогой: the г changes.
items.explanation: Дороже is the irregular synthetic comparative of дорогой: the stem-final г changes to ж, suffix -е.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is taller than his brother.
items.hint: Irregular synthetic comparative of высокий, with a bare-genitive 'than'.
items.explanation: Выше is the irregular synthetic comparative of высокий (the stem высок- shortens to выш-). Here we compare two people, so we need the comparative выше plus the bare genitive брата.

items.promptEnglish: This is a more interesting book than that one.
items.hint: The comparative sits before the noun книга. Which form can agree?
items.explanation: Before a noun only the compound form works, and it must agree: более интересная (feminine, to match книга). The synthetic интереснее is invariable and cannot sit before a noun.

items.promptEnglish: This is the most beautiful house in the city.
items.hint: Superlative with the masculine noun дом.
items.explanation: Самый красивый is the everyday superlative; самый agrees with the masculine дом (-ый).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This article is more interesting than that one.
minimalPairs.explanation: Predicative slot after the subject favours the synthetic form in everyday speech: интереснее, invariable. Более интересная is grammatical here but feels heavy; it is the required form only before a noun (attributive position).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This is a more interesting article in the magazine.
minimalPairs.explanation: The comparative sits before the noun статья, so only the compound form works: более интересная, agreeing in the feminine. The invariable one-word интереснее cannot stand before a noun.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This bread is better than that one.
minimalPairs.explanation: Хороший has a memorised comparative, лучше ('better'). Более хороший ('more good') is a calque Russian rejects, since the single word лучше already exists. Pick the irregular synthetic word, not the compound.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each form into the construction it belongs to.

errorCorrection.sentence: Этот компьютер более лучше, чем тот.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This computer is better than that one.
errorCorrection.explanation: Лучше already means 'better', so putting более in front of it stacks two markers, the classic double-comparative error. Use the single word лучше.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is a more interesting book than that one.
errorCorrection.explanation: Before a noun the comparative must agree, and only the compound form can: более интересная книга (feminine, to match книга). The synthetic интереснее is invariable and cannot stand before a noun.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is the oldest in the class.
errorCorrection.explanation: In the superlative самый is itself a declining word and must agree with the noun, just like the adjective. Маша is feminine, so both words take the feminine: самая старшая.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is the most interesting film of the year.
errorCorrection.explanation: Интереснейший is already a one-word literary superlative ('most interesting'), so adding самый doubles the superlative. The everyday form is самый + the plain adjective: самый интересный.

blanks: Антон на два года _____ своего брата. (Anton is two years older than his brother.)
Это _____ дом на нашей улице. (This is the most beautiful house on our street.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Blank 1: the irregular synthetic comparative старше (старый → старше, formed with the suffix -ше, not the regular -ее), with the gap phrase 'на два года' and the bare genitive брата. Blank 2: the superlative самый красивый, where самый agrees with the masculine дом.

reviewVocab.definition: regular synthetic comparatives: stem + -ее, one fixed form that never changes (новый → новее, интересный → интереснее)
reviewVocab.example: Этот дом новее, а эта книга интереснее.

reviewVocab.definition: irregular synthetic comparatives: stem + -е with a changed consonant, memorised not built (хороший → лучше, дорогой → дороже, высокий → выше)
reviewVocab.example: Кофе дороже чая, и эта книга лучше той.

reviewVocab.definition: the compound comparative: более 'more' or менее 'less' + an agreeing adjective; the only comparative that can sit before a noun
reviewVocab.example: Это более интересная книга, а тот фильм менее интересный.

reviewVocab.definition: the everyday superlative: самый 'the most' + an agreeing adjective (the formal наиболее / наименее mean the same and are recognise-only)
reviewVocab.example: Это самый красивый дом, а Маша — самая старшая в классе.
